title: Surprises & Gotchas
lead: The clever, the subtle, and the watch-outs.
summary: A curated, cross-cutting collection of the highest-signal findings in MemPalace: non-obvious design choices, clever patterns, and the traps that bite without warning. Every entry is traced to a real line of code and grouped into insights, gotchas, performance, and security. It is where the verbatim-always, local-first, never-corrupt philosophy meets the messy reality of ChromaDB internals, cross-platform shells, Unicode boundaries, and weak local LLMs.

searchDoc.title: Surprises & Gotchas
searchDoc.summary: The highest-signal cross-cutting page: curated insights, gotchas, performance notes, and security findings from across MemPalace, each traced to a line of code.
searchDoc.body: This page aggregates the most surprising, non-obvious, and watch-out findings across MemPalace, grouped into four kinds and each traceable to source. Key insights: raw verbatim text beats LLM-extracted memory by roughly 2x on LongMemEval (96.6% R@5 vs 30-45% for extraction systems like Mem0) because extraction discards context and loses the original when it fails. Closets are a ranking signal that only boosts, never a gate that filters, so weak closets can only help search. The corpus-origin pipeline treats the local LLM as a scalpel, discarding its verdict when it disagrees with a confident regex heuristic. BM25 IDF is computed over the candidate set rather than the corpus, which is correct for discriminating within results. Date-only knowledge-graph facts are normalized into full-day intervals at query time. The fact-checker uses two regexes rather than NLP to stay ultra-conservative, preferring false-negatives to false-positives. Gotchas: a per-thread re-entrant lock prevents the mine pipeline from deadlocking against itself; macOS bash 3.2 cannot use mapfile so the hook parses with sed; Windows cannot probe a PID with os.kill(pid,0) and uses GetExitCodeProcess; Python's word boundary truncates names with Unicode combining marks; switching embedding models silently breaks a palace via name mismatch, and legacy palaces silently default to L2 distance breaking cosine scores; KG predicates are lowercased and foreign keys are soft constraints; RTF bypasses MarkItDown for striprtf; init is made idempotent only by filtering its own artifacts. Performance: ChromaDB silently truncates at 10K rows so metadata is paginated; absolute cosine keeps ranking stable; the HNSW divergence floor scales with the sync threshold; emotion detection is keyword-based and zero-token; the Stop hook runs async while PreCompact runs sync. Security: MCP stdio is redirected at the file-descriptor level before heavy imports because C libraries write to fd 1; the pickle health check sniff-tests bytes without deserializing; non-HTTP LLM endpoints are rejected at parse time to block file exfiltration; the query sanitizer turns a silent recall cliff from system-prompt contamination into a graceful 70-89% degradation.
